status: PASS: frozen-control bounds and 256 native diagnostic costs
question: How much of the old Qwen38 whole-row improvement survives arbitrary scheduling of the same frozen control jobs?

data.source: Previously used external-doc-grounded-stride1-short routes; no new dataset, fit, labels, or heldout task.

proof: For each chip, sum the mandatory ordinary-read duration of its frozen selected jobs, including shared jobs. Reads on a single chip are serialized under the stated one-context ordinary-read contract. This gives the NAND-only lower bound max_chip sum_job waves*tR, regardless of expert/phase job order. No controller, host, input, output, or PCIe cost is needed for this lower bound.

For the fixed postcompute-output-drain DAG, chip ownership covers command, full input channel transfer, all ordinary-read waves, and all-page-fringe output channel drain. PCIe output is excluded from ownership. Thus host_initial + max_chip sum_owned is a lower bound. Serialized controller work, channel work, PCIe work, host work, and causal longest paths supply additional valid bounds; take their maximum.

The broader streaming relaxation replaces job read+output_channel by max(read,output_channel), drops the postcompute-drain causal path, and permits duplex PCIe. It retains full-input reload, mandatory job transfers, and one held chip context per job. It is not a proof of a specific native streaming implementation.

Each layer is a causal FFN step. Summing its per-query lower bound across 48 layers lower-bounds the aggregate FFN service for that token. This is not complete LLM wall time and does not add attention, routing, or inter-layer work.

A free control relaxation takes min(LB_g16,LB_groupbest,LB_overlap) separately for every layer/query, then sums 48 layers. This grants cost-free selection among three frozen copies/geometries and is therefore optimistic for those controls. It says nothing about unenumerated geometries, labels, command coalescing, native caching, or retiling.
geometry_and_IO: Jobs and their order come from the original frozen plan and variant array, including fixed shared FFN. No lower_rows order is substituted. The coverage check verifies a complete nonoverlapping whole-row output range and full column range.

For each job p=ceil(rows*C/16384), waves=ceil(p/4), mode1 output_rows=floor(p*16384/C). Every whole-page-fringe output transfer is paid. Input size is actual per-expert/projection C times input_bytes, not Qwen constants. Common GU input dimension is explicitly checked across routed and shared experts.

Ordinary-read service is 28000ns/wave, command 250ns, host submission 2000ns, one-byte input and four-byte output. These are frozen model assumptions, not new measured hardware calibration. See protocol for every parameter.

validation.bulk: Independent vectorized ledgers; all 3 bounds checked <= original saved feasible cost for every one of 264912 layer/query records per control and whole. All frozen input hashes rechecked after run.

optional_EPYC_copy.meaning: Rounded observed P99 of a separate one-thread EPYC host F32 row-gather streaming benchmark. Whole-only scenario, not mandatory DMA tax or hardware worst-case guarantee. No addition to controls; no 48x repetition.

limits: Positive margins certify only the named frozen jobs/control set and service contracts. They do not establish a globally optimal cyclic baseline, any new theorem, nor a universal hardware speedup.
The old whole-row feasible cost remains the uncalibrated software replay. Controller-parameter sensitivity elsewhere reverses the comparison near 5us; this study does not remove that limitation.

Native AiF output dtype, numerical scale contract, MAC throughput, intra-job streaming, and direct scatter-DMA behavior remain unverified. The NAND-only control relaxation minimizes dependency on these assumptions but cannot validate the whole feasible hardware implementation.

Root v3 geometry alias/search-budget attribution issue is a separate later campaign. This study uses the earlier frozen native-full48 plans, fixed variant inventory, old mode1 outputs, and no refitting.
sources: No new literature search required for this bounded code/data audit; inputs and source hashes are in protocol.frozen.json.
